notes: Recorded from the seven UCT faculty pages that list postgraduate degrees: 315 master's rows and 95 doctoral rows (one row per programme and faculty: the same programme in several degree types of one faculty is merged, with the degree types in the detail). The pages state no total. The Faculty of Health Sciences page names the doctoral degrees MD, PhD and DSc(Med) without majors, so those are recorded as degrees.
Not recorded: Honours degrees (the scholarship also supports one year of Honours), postgraduate diplomas, postgraduate certificates and the PGCE, because they are not master's or doctoral levels.

UCT's 2027 funding handbook says, for its own merit and need awards, that candidates in the fourth year of a bachelor's degree, the PGCE, postgraduate diplomas, other part-time programmes, and the LLB and BArch are not eligible for postgraduate funding. It does not state these exclusions for the international and refugee scholarships specifically, so professional or part-time master's programmes may be affected; check with the Postgraduate Funding Office.
The same handbook says people employed full time (more than 20 hours a week) are not eligible, and that funding cannot extend to third-year master's and fourth-year doctoral students.
A source spelling error is kept as published (Clincial Paediatric Surgery).
